clue.text: It includes " Nude Mp " terribly saucy!

indicators.note: includes means the word It holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters of Nude Mp are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A newspaper caption about a naked politician, condemned as shockingly cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges NUDE MP to MPUDEN, which 'includes' puts inside IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucy and the answer both describe cheeky, disrespectful boldness.

clue.text: Unskilled to rebuild pier next

indicators.note: to rebuild means the letters of pier next are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Workmen unqualified to reconstruct the neighbouring jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: Unskilled means lacking expertise or competence.

clue.text: Fields older than you, might one say ?

indicators.note: might one say asks us to listen to how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: someone older than you is beyond your age in years

explanation.surface: A sly question about ageing compared to another person.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase PAST YOUR AGE, said quickly, sounds like the word for grazing land.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasturage is land used for grazing, that is, grassy fields.

clue.text: Southern Us vessel

explanation.surface: A ship from the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: Dixie is the nickname for the US South; a dixie is also a large army cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Dixie names the American South, and a dixie is also a soldier's cooking pot or mess tin.

clue.text: Getting close to one leaving N Nigeria in chaos "

indicators.note: in chaos means the letters N and Nigeria are thrown together in disorder

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Approaching a figure fleeing northern Nigeria during turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I (one) out of the letters of N plus NIGERIA, and 'in chaos' mixes the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearing means approaching or drawing close to something.

clue.text: County personnel?

explanation.surface: A wry query about the staff of a shire council.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffordshire, an English Midlands county, is abbreviated this way, and a firm's personnel are its employees.

clue.text: Number of promissory notes: about a bill — tough

parts.note: ten is a number
a/c, an account, is a bill
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Counting IOUs around an invoice, a hard business.
explanation.walkthrough: AC (a/c, short for account) goes inside IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough in the sense of stubborn and persistent, refusing to let go.

clue.text: Tuck in here, cook said

indicators.note: said signals that the word for a cook is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a fryer is one who fries, a cook

explanation.surface: An invitation to eat, spoken by a chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck in here' looks like a call to eat; it means the slot before Tuck, as in Robin Hood's Friar Tuck.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood's companion is named Friar Tuck, so this title fills the gap before Tuck.

clue.text: Run-that's the ticket.

explanation.surface: Someone urging another to hurry because it is the right thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a single is one run; a single is also a one-way ticket in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A single is one run in cricket, and also a one-way rail ticket.

clue.text: How the wicket-keeper baffles you

parts.note: in cricket the keeper gets a batsman out by breaking the wicket while he is out of his ground; the same verb means puzzles

explanation.surface: A complaint about being outwitted by the gloveman in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The wicket-keeper stands behind the batsman in cricket; dismissing him by knocking the bails off is the verb that also means perplexes.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to dismiss a batsman this way and to perplex or confound.

clue.text: Letters said' to identify an earl

indicators.note: said tells us the letters are to be spoken by their names

parts.note: the letters S and X, named aloud as 'ess' and 'ex'

explanation.surface: Correspondence read out as proof of a nobleman's identity.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying the letter names S and X gives the sound of the title; the Earl of Essex was Elizabeth I's favourite. ESSEX is also an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Essex is a famous peer, so the title stands for an earl.

clue.text: Standing order?

parts.note: looks like a banking instruction for regular payments, but is read as a drill command telling soldiers to stand still and upright

explanation.surface: A bank's regular-payment instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The parade-ground command to stand rigidly still is literally an order about standing.

clue.text: Without a penny, I'm sure Pa is embarrassed by it

indicators.note: embarrassed here means thrown into confusion, so the letters of I'm sure Pa are jumbled

explanation.surface: A child, confident that a broke father feels ashamed of being poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is embarrassed' jumbles I'M SURE PA into AUPERISM, after P for 'penny'; 'it' points back to the state of having no money, so the clue is nearly all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's 'it' refers to the condition of being penniless, which is destitution or poverty.

clue.text: She finds' nothing right, back in California

indicators.note: in means the reversed pair sits inside the abbreviation for the state
back means the two letters for nothing and right are read in reverse order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman discovers there is no justice on returning to California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OR into RO, which goes 'in' CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it can stand for any woman, she.

clue.text: Study concerning a tail-less Australian dog

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: tail-less says the dog's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the dingo is Australia's wild dog

explanation.surface: Research about a dingo that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail-less' cuts DINGO to DING.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is a form of study, as in a scholar's reading of a text.

clue.text: Self-styled paragon tense

parts.note: a self-styled person describes himself with I am, contracted to I'm
a paragon is flawless, perfect

explanation.surface: A conceited person who claims perfection is uptight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-styled paragon' is someone saying I'M PERFECT; 'tense' is grammar, not nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar this is the past tense of continuing action, 'I was going'.

clue.text: Vessels where invalid diet includes duck

indicators.note: includes means the sick person's food holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: slops are the weak liquid food given to an invalid
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: Bowls of hospital food containing duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: These single-masted sailing boats are vessels.

clue.text: Whereby fairies manage to overlook things ?

definitions.text: Whereby fairies manage to overlook things

parts.note: peris are fairies of Persian myth
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Asking how little winged folk contrive to see over obstacles.
explanation.walkthrough: A peri is a fairy in Persian legend; the whole clue also describes the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's optical tube lets its user see over obstacles, so it is a means of overlooking things.

clue.text: Lovely ladies, but so careless with crockery

explanation.surface: Attractive women who keep breaking the dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashers' is old British slang for very attractive people.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for stunningly attractive people, and literally those who break plates and cups.

clue.text: Hesperus — more than one in service

explanation.surface: The evening star counted among a congregation at worship.
explanation.walkthrough: Hesperus, the Latin evening star, has this as its other name; with an S added it is the evening church service, so a single one is 'more than one' short.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the Latin for evening: the evening star, and evensong, the evening office, whose name is plural.

clue.text: This map of Lucknow?

parts.note: a kind of map showing hills and valleys, and also the event of 1857 when the besieged Indian city was rescued

explanation.surface: A query about a chart of an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Siege of Lucknow in the 1857 Indian Rebellion ended with its famous rescue; a map showing raised terrain shares the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A map showing land elevation bears this name, as did the 1857 lifting of the siege of Lucknow.

clue.text: It's a sin to drink for five years

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins
rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Drinking is condemned as sinful for half a decade.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman lustrum was the five-year period between censuses.

clue.text: Appear socially acceptable to Taffy, see ?

parts.note: to look is to appear or seem
U means upper-class, socially acceptable, and the letter is named 'you'

explanation.surface: A Welshman remarking that someone seems respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Taffy' marks a Welsh turn of phrase: 'look you' is the stage Welshman's 'see?' Taffy is an old nickname for a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock Welsh tag means 'mark this', just as the speaker's see does.

clue.text: East's raising proper respect

parts.note: E for East, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: raising, in a down clue, means the word for proper is read upwards

parts.note: meet is an old word for proper or fitting

explanation.surface: Those in the East insisting on due respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns MEET into TEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold in esteem is to regard with respect and admiration.

clue.text: Sister "Susie's connexion with building development

parts.note: Sister Susie of the old song sews shirts for soldiers, so she is one who sews; a new building development needs a connexion to the drains

explanation.surface: A nun's relationship to a property scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister Susie's Sewing Shirts for Soldiers' was a First World War music-hall song; the word for one who sews is spelt like the drain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who sews and the underground drain a new building is connected to.

clue.text: ""A little clears us of this deed " (Macbeth)

definitions.text: "A little clears us of this deed " (Macbeth)

parts.words: "A little clears us of this deed " (Macbeth)
parts.note: Lady Macbeth's line after the murder, telling her husband to wash the blood off his hands

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's tragedy with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Macbeth says a little of the washing liquid will clean their hands of the murder.

clue.text: Stories about one ship, such as Elsa

indicators.note: about means the falsehoods surround the following letters

parts.note: stories as in fibs, untruths
taken as written
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Tales concerning a single boat, for example the one called Elsa.
explanation.walkthrough: Elsa was the lioness raised by Joy Adamson in Born Free.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsa is the famous example of a female big cat, so 'such as Elsa' means animals of that kind.

clue.text: Send down to invest a small sum in fish

indicators.note: in places the small sum inside the fish's name

parts.note: an eel is a fish
X is ten and P pence, so XP is ten pence, a small sum

explanation.surface: Advice to put a little money into a fish business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send down' is the British university term for expelling a student.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sent down from university is to be expelled.

clue.text: Most unhappily met Rex in the City

indicators.note: unhappily signals that the letters of met Rex are put in a sorry jumble

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A sad encounter with a king in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' rearranges MET REX into EXTREM. Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Most, used as an intensifier ('most kind'), means very greatly.

clue.text: Quiet girl-not in 'the Sonnets

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, meaning quietly
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A shy young woman who does not appear in Shakespeare's poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Sonnets are verse, and ordinary writing that is not verse is the opposite.

clue.text: Deserts King Edward in the swirling mist

indicators.note: in places the royal letters inside the whirled mist
swirling means the letters of mist are churned around

parts.note: ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A monarch abandoning his post in a fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' turns MIST into MITS, with ER put 'in'. 'Deserts' is what one deserves (just deserts), not wastelands or abandoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserts in 'just deserts' are what one deserves, one's worth or dues.

clue.text: Smith's epicure's postprandial state

parts.note: the condition of a gourmet after a big dinner, his stomach well stuffed; Smith hints at a quotation

explanation.surface: How a gourmet feels after dinner, as described by a writer named Smith.
explanation.walkthrough: Postprandial means after a meal; the gourmet's state then is one of satiety.
explanation.definitionFit: After dining an epicure is replete, so satiety describes the condition.
